title: Graphing a Shifted Absolute Value Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = |1 - x| - 1 by rewriting it in standard vertex form and finding its vertex, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Rewrite Using Symmetry of Absolute Value
steps.explanation: Because |-u| = |u| for all real u, |1 - x| is identical to |x - 1|. Thus the graph is obtained by shifting y = |x| right 1 unit and down 1 unit.
steps.why: The absolute value property |-u| = |u| simplifies |1 - x| to standard horizontal shift form |x - 1|.

steps.title: Identify the Vertex, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: Since |x - 1| >= 0 with equality at x = 1, the minimum value is y = -1 at the vertex (1, -1), and the range is [-1, infinity).
steps.why: Subtracting 1 from the non-negative quantity |x - 1| shifts the minimum output from 0 to -1.

steps.title: Determine the x- and y-Intercepts
steps.explanation: The V-shaped graph crosses the origin (0, 0) and (2, 0) with slopes -1 for x < 1 and +1 for x > 1.
steps.why: Solving |x - 1| = 1 yields the two points at distance 1 from x = 1.
